title: Ledger
description: Per-task run ledger written by deterministic code (shared-node/ledger.mjs). Must agree with validateLedger.

gitConfigHash.description: sha256 of the bytes of .pairingbuddy/git-config.json recorded at pb run open, after the file is bootstrapped. May be absent on ledgers written before it existed.

startedAt.description: ISO 8601 time the gate last marked this stage active, or null. May be absent.

runId.description: Identifies this pb run (task) for its whole life; written once by pb run open and never changed. Not the same as stage.runId, which is the workflow run of the current stage attempt. May be absent on older ledgers.

checkpoints.description: Each pb checkpoint that went through, a step with no change included. May be absent.

askedAt.description: When gate eval asked the question: the wait on the human starts here and is no working time. May be absent (ledgers written before it).

shown.description: What gate eval showed the human at G:publish: the HEAD sha, the unit base and the PR target. May be absent. A publish answer is refused if HEAD is no longer headSha.

question.description: The question gate eval issued for this gate, exactly as the human is asked it. May be absent. The hooks record an answer only to this question.

wait.description: Marks a question that is no answer to the gate itself, such as go-on: whether to go on past the human's own stop at that gate. The tap records its answer as that wait. May be absent.

fix.description: What the views show under a wait the session asks about outside the gates, such as a changed test-config: answer the question, or the ! line to type when it cannot be asked. May be absent.

doubts.description: The open doubts the question names, in full (the question shows at most three, each whole on one line, and run/question.md holds them all), each with the plain name of the step that had it, so the run report holds them all. A reviewer's doubt also names the stage it reviewed (stage), so the report can say which review raised it. May be absent.

options.description: Answers the step suggested for its doubt, which /pb-questions offers as choices. May be absent.

gateWaits.description: Answered gate questions whose gate record is gone (a redo removes it) or replaced (an approval over a stop), oldest first, so the time the human spent answering stays waiting, no working time. A record still in gates keeps its own askedAt and answeredAt. May be absent.

stopWaits.description: Each stop of the run, oldest first: when it was set (askedAt) and, once lifted, when (answeredAt). A stopped run does no work, so the time is waiting, as a question's is. The ledger write sets them. May be absent.

idleWaits.description: Each gap of more than an hour between two ledger writes, oldest first: from the last write (askedAt) to the write that ended it (answeredAt). Every step, test run and owner's tool call writes the ledger, so nothing ran then (a night, a closed session). The ledger write sets them. May be absent.

permissionWaits.description: Claude Code's own permission prompts that stood unanswered during the run, oldest first: hooks/permission.mjs opens one on the prompt's Notification (notification_type permission_prompt) and closes it with answeredAt on the next tool call, the turn's end or the human's next prompt. The last one, while it has no answeredAt, is open: the run needs the human. The time from askedAt to answeredAt (or to now, while open) is waiting, no working time. May be absent.

seq.description: The ledger seq the wait was opened at, so the alert fires once for it.

tool.description: The tool the prompt asks for, as Claude Code names it. May be absent.

voidedGates.description: Gate approvals that stopped holding (G:publish after HEAD or the body moved), oldest first, kept for the audit trail. May be absent. record is the gate record as it stood; reason says what changed.

lenses.description: Lens records by name (the one the publish gate reads is "safety-net"). `pb stage finish` on a safety-net stage writes "safety-net": the stage, the attempt, the lenses that ran with their models, the counts of surviving, refuted and unrefuted findings, and the names of uncovered lenses. It holds no finding content. May be absent.

fixes.description: Fix bookkeeping. rollbacks lists each rolled-back fix group, oldest first: its key, kind (commit, red, artifact, repeated for a fix that repeated an approach already rolled back, or hook for a fix the repo's commit hook refused), the rollback ref that keeps the rejected work, sha (the commit that ref points at: the fix commit, or the commit holding the saved dirty paths), and base (HEAD after the rollback). ref is a string for kind commit, red or hook, and for kind repeated when the fix changed something; it is null for kind artifact, which records no git ref, and for kind repeated when the fix changed nothing. hookRefusals lists each fix whose commit the repo's commit hook refused: its key and the hook's output, which its rollback note carries. May be absent; when present it has rollbacks, and hookRefusals once a hook refused a fix.

removed.description: Untracked files the fix created without listing them (a sed backup, say), removed by the rollback and kept under ref. Absent when there were none.

untrackedAtStart.description: The untracked files present when the stage's snapshot ran (stage and attempt name it). A rollback of that stage and attempt removes any untracked file not listed here, keeping it under a rollback ref, and never touches a listed one. Absent when the snapshot found more than MAX_UNTRACKED_BASELINE files, so no untracked file counts as the fix's.

acceptances.description: Each hand edit a human accepted with pb human accept, oldest first. May be absent. oldSha is the sha the edited file carried; newSha is the sha of the content as edited, before the acceptance was added; seq is the seq the acceptance wrote.

configAcceptances.description: Each changed test-config a human accepted with pb human accept, oldest first. May be absent. oldHash is the configHash the run held, newHash the one it holds from then on, and seq the seq the acceptance wrote.

guidance.description: How the curating-guidance skill left human-guidance.json before this run opened: mode auto when nobody was asked (auto mode, claude -p, or nothing changed), human when the human approved; kept and dropped count the entries. May be absent.
